articles.title: Kimberly Powell: quem é a executiva da Nvidia ligada a Jensen Huang | G1
articles.standfirst: Powell é vice-presidente da área de saúde da empresa de tecnologia. Reportagem do jornal 'The New York Times' revela um relacionamento dela com o ex-CEO Jensen Huang.
articles.summary: Kimberly Powell, vice-presidente de saúde da Nvidia, é citada em novo escândalo com Jensen Huang que já custou US$ 1 trilhão em valor de mercado à empresa.
articles.body:
Kimberly Powell, vice-presidente da área de saúde da Nvidia, que teria se relacionado com CEO da empresa. — Foto: Kimberly Powell/Reprodução

O ex-presidente-executivo da Nvidia , Jensen Huang , também teria mantido um relacionamento extraconjugal com Kimberly Powell, executiva da empresa que responde diretamente a ele. A informação foi revelada pelo jornal "The New York Times".

Huang está no centro de uma crise na companhia após admitir um caso extraconjugal. Ainda segundo a imprensa estrangeira, ela seria Alice Huang, acusada de espionagem para a China. Ele renunciou ao comando da empresa nesta quinta-feira (12).

Powell, de 48 anos, é vice-presidente da área de saúde da Nvidia, uma das maiores empresas de tecnologia do mundo e principal fornecedora de chips usados no desenvolvimento de inteligência artificial.

De acordo com o jornal, Huang e Powell teriam sido vistos em uma situação de intimidade em um hotel de San Jose, na Califórnia, durante uma conferência da empresa, em março. (saiba mais abaixo)

As alegações não foram confirmadas publicamente por Powell, Huang ou pela Nvidia. O episódio, no entanto, colocou a executiva no centro de uma discussão sobre governança corporativa e possíveis conflitos de interesse, já que ela se reportava diretamente ao CEO.

Após a publicação da reportagem, Powell cancelou sua participação como painelista no "Future of Health Summit", evento organizado pelo Milken Institute, em Washington.

Kimberly Powell trabalha na Nvidia há mais de 18 anos. Formada em Engenharia Elétrica, com concentração em Engenharia de Computação, pela Northeastern University, nos Estados Unidos, Powell construiu sua carreira na intersecção entre tecnologia e medicina.

Antes de chegar à Nvidia, trabalhou em empresas ligadas ao desenvolvimento de equipamentos e sistemas de diagnóstico por imagem . Nessas companhias, acumulou experiência em engenharia e gerenciamento de produtos voltados à radiologia e à área de saúde.

Powell ingressou na Nvidia em maio de 2008. Inicialmente, sua missão era desenvolver oportunidades de negócios nos setores de saúde e ensino superior, ajudando a posicionar as unidades de processamento gráfico (GPUs) da empresa como plataformas de aceleração computacional para equipamentos médicos, especialmente os utilizados em exames de diagnóstico por imagem.

Ao longo de sua trajetória na Nvidia, Powell também esteve à frente de iniciativas de aproximação da empresa com universidades, pesquisadores e empresas emergentes de tecnologia. Entre os projetos que liderou estão o NVIDIA AI Labs, voltado à colaboração com pesquisadores e instituições acadêmicas, e o NVIDIA Inception, programa de apoio a startups que desenvolvem soluções de inteligência artificial.

Em outubro de 2017, assumiu a vice-presidência global da área de Healthcare, cargo que ocupa desde então. A executiva passou a comandar a estratégia da Nvidia para o setor de saúde, que envolve o desenvolvimento e a aplicação de inteligência artificial, computação acelerada e robótica em diferentes atividades médicas e científicas .

Entre as frentes de atuação estão diagnóstico por imagem, análise genômica, descoberta de medicamentos e desenvolvimento de tecnologias para pesquisas biomédicas.

Como uma das principais representantes da Nvidia no setor, Powell também participa de conferências internacionais da indústria, incluindo a GTC, principal evento da companhia.

No início desta semana, Jensen Huang havia admitido ter mantido outro relacionamento extraconjugal, desta vez com a executiva chinesa Alice Huang . O caso teria provocado uma crise na Nvidia, em meio a suspeitas de que ela atuasse como agente de espionagem para o governo chinês.

Alice foi executiva da Megaspeed, empresa de data centers sediada em Singapura e uma das maiores clientes da Nvidia no Sudeste Asiático.

O conselho de administração da Nvidia chegou a abrir uma investigação para apurar possíveis riscos à segurança das informações da companhia, à cadeia de fornecimento de chips avançados de IA e à segurança nacional dos EUA.

O novo caso envolvendo Huang se soma às preocupações sobre a empresa. Segundo levantamento da Elos Ayta, a companhia havia perdido até ontem US$ 1,081 trilhão (cerca de R$ 6,1 trilhões) em valor de mercado no período em que começaram a surgir as informações sobre o executivo.

Segundo o jornal "The Wall Street Journal", o conselho estaria agora se preparando para destituir Jensen Huang do cargo de presidente-executivo em meio à repercussão dos dois casos.

Jensen Huang, CEO da Nvidia, durante evento em Washington — Foto: Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo

Kimberly Powell entrou na Nvidia em 2008 e construiu sua carreira na companhia. Em 2016, foi promovida a diretora sênior de desenvolvimento de negócios em inteligência artificial e, no fim de 2017, assumiu a vice-presidência da área de saúde.

Ela coordena iniciativas que levam a tecnologia dos chips da Nvidia a áreas como saúde e ensino superior, incluindo aplicações em equipamentos de diagnóstico por imagem.

Segundo o jornal, um suposto relacionamento entre Huang e Powell já era comentado internamente na Nvidia. O código de conduta da empresa orienta os funcionários a evitar situações que possam gerar conflitos de interesse, incluindo relacionamentos pessoais.

Em março, durante a conferência anual de desenvolvedores da Nvidia, em San Jose, Powell fez uma apresentação sobre como a inteligência artificial pode contribuir para avanços na saúde e na biologia.

Durante o evento, executivos da companhia também participaram de reuniões em um hotel próximo, onde Huang e Powell teriam sido vistos juntos.

O jornal diz que, de acordo com três pessoas que tiveram conhecimento do episódio, um funcionário que presenciou a interação durante a convenção teria gravado a cena com o celular. A equipe de segurança de Huang teria percebido a gravação e retirado o funcionário do local.

Em seguida, a equipe de Huang teria oferecido ao funcionário um acordo de confidencialidade, documento que limita a divulgação de determinadas informações. O jornal "The New York Times" afirma não ter visto o vídeo que teria registrado o encontro.

Por que as traições representam um problema tão sério para o executivo?

Até o momento, entre os dois relacionamentos extraconjugais revelados, o primeiro é o que traz consequências potencialmente mais graves para Jensen Huang .

Isso porque o caso ultrapassa a esfera pessoal e envolve questões de segurança nacional e os negócios da empresa. China e Estados Unidos disputam a liderança no setor de tecnologia, especialmente no desenvolvimento de inteligência artificial.

Nesse cenário, o governo americano impõe restrições à exportação de chips avançados para o mercado chinês. A Nvidia, líder mundial na fabricação desses processadores, está diretamente envolvida nessa disputa, já que seus produtos são fundamentais para o desenvolvimento da tecnologia.

articles.title: Colette Kress, Ian Buck and five others who could be Nvidia’s next CEO as the company prepares to fire Jensen Huang
articles.summary: Nvidia has never had to think seriously about who comes after Jensen Huang.
articles.body: Nvidia has never had to think seriously about who comes after Jensen Huang. He co-founded the company in 1993, has been its only chief executive since, and built it so completely around himself that succession always felt like a question for some distant year. That year may have arrived this week.On November 8, the chipmaker's board opened an independent investigation following reports that Huang, 63, had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The New York Times had reported on October 29 that Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Singapore-based Nvidia customer Megaspeed, sought to cultivate close ties with him, and both the Times and the Financial Times reported that US intelligence agencies suspect she was passing information to Beijing. In an email to staff on November 8, Huang admitted to the affair. China has dismissed the allegations as a smear. The board said it still had confidence in him, and on November 10 it hired Joon H. Kim, a former acting US attorney for the Southern District of New York, at law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead the probe.By November 11, the mood had turned. The New York Times reported that Huang had also been in a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare and one of his direct reports. Minutes later, The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to force him out. Directors met late into the night, shares fell more than 9% in after-hours trading, and Bloomberg reported that the board is working with an outside firm to explore replacements. At the time of writing, the company has not announced a decision.Under the company's bylaws, a majority of directors can replace the CEO without cause. The harder part is finding the name that goes in his place.Nvidia’s flat structure left no obvious successor to Jensen HuangJensen Huang runs one of the flattest structures in big tech. He had 55 direct reports in 2024 and 36 by late 2025, and he skips one-on-one meetings so that every leader hears the same thing at the same time. Asked about succession, he has said there will "never be one like me," while arguing that the dozens of executives around him could each run a company of their own because they have watched him make every decision.That design kept Nvidia fast. It also means nobody below Huang has ever held a view of the whole company. The bench got thinner in August, when Jay Puri, who ran worldwide sales for two decades, retired and handed over to former Microsoft executive Nick Parker.These are the seven names now in the frame, two of them from Huang's own family.Colette Kress is the safest pair of hands for the interim jobKress has been chief financial officer since 2013. Before that she was CFO of Cisco's business technology and operations finance organisation, and spent 13 years at Microsoft, the last four as CFO of its Server and Tools division, after starting out in finance at Texas Instruments. After Huang, she is the executive investors know best, the voice that has walked Wall Street through every quarter of the AI boom, including a fiscal 2026 in which revenue grew 65% to $215.9 billion. Semafor reported that some directors favour naming her interim CEO.The doubt is about what comes after. Her entire career has been in finance, and analysts do not see her as a natural successor to Huang's role as the company's technology visionary. As a stabiliser while the board searches, though, no one else is as ready. She already owns the numbers the market is holding the company to, including her own forecast of 70% revenue growth in fiscal 2028.Ian Buck has the strongest claim among the engineersBuck created CUDA, the software platform that made Nvidia's GPUs the default choice for AI work and that rivals still struggle to match. The idea began at Stanford, where his PhD work produced Brook, an early attempt at running general-purpose code on graphics chips, and Nvidia hired him in 2004 to turn it into a product. In roughly 22 years at the company, he has risen to run hyperscale and high-performance computing, the heart of the data centre business that now brings in most of its revenue. His job puts him in daily contact with Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta and OpenAI.Bettors on Polymarket have him as favourite for the permanent role. He also brings something this moment needs, having testified before the US Congress on AI and advised the White House. Some analysts have floated a shared interim arrangement, with Kress handling the finances and Buck the technology and customer relationships. The open question is whether a product leader who has never run the whole company can carry its public face the way Huang did.Rene Haas is the outsider who already knows the cultureHaas has been CEO of Arm since 2022, but before that he spent seven years at Nvidia, rising to run its computing products business. He took Arm public in 2023, and in March he moved it beyond licensing designs to selling its own chip for the first time, a data centre processor called the AGI CPU, with Meta as its first customer. Few outsiders combine first-hand knowledge of how Huang operates with experience steering a listed chip company through that kind of change.Futurum Group analyst Shay Boloor wrote on X that if he had to bet on an external pick, it would be Haas. Polymarket odds on him have since dropped sharply, and the timing works against him. Having just put Arm into competition with some of its own customers, Nvidia among them, he would be walking away from the biggest bet of his tenure.Johny Srouji would bring Apple's chip disciplineSrouji led Apple's in-house silicon programme from its first chip, the A4, in 2008, through to the processors that now power every iPhone and Mac, and his group went on to take over batteries, cameras, displays and Apple's own cellular modems. Before Apple, he worked on processor design at Intel and IBM. In April, Apple made him chief hardware officer, placing its entire hardware engineering organisation under him as John Ternus prepared to take over from Tim Cook.His name has come up as a possible external successor. On paper, he offers what Kress cannot: an engineer who built a chip team from scratch inside a company that had never designed its own processors. The difficulty is timing. He has only just been handed the largest role of his career in Cupertino, which would make him hard to lure away.Eric Schmidt is the caretaker some would reach forThe former Google CEO is the least conventional name here, and he already has a job: since March 2025 he has been CEO and controlling shareholder of rocket maker Relativity Space. Still, Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of the Yale School of Management, who advises chief executives and boards, has said he has heard Schmidt rumoured as a possible choice and that Schmidt "could step in tomorrow and do a very good job."Schmidt ran Google from 2001 to 2011, taking it from a fast-growing search company to a global giant, and has since spent years on AI and national security policy in Washington. That last part matters now. A board dealing with a spy investigation, congressional pressure and nervous shareholders may value a calm, well-connected figure more than an engineer, at least for a while.Madison Huang is the family name with the most visible riseJensen Huang's daughter took a route into technology unlike anyone else on this list. She trained at The Culinary Institute of America and Le Cordon Bleu, cooked in restaurant kitchens, then spent close to four years at LVMH marketing champagne brands such as Dom Pérignon and Veuve Clicquot. In 2019 she started an MBA at London Business School and took a short AI course at MIT, and in 2020 she joined Nvidia as a marketing intern. She is now senior director of product and technical marketing for the company's physical AI platforms, including Omniverse, Cosmos and Isaac.Her growing number of public appearances with her father, including at the World Robot Conference in Beijing in August, has fed talk that she is being prepared for more, and former employees have said her influence reaches beyond her formal marketing role. Still, Nvidia's 2026 proxy filing shows she is not an executive officer and does not report directly to her father. Huang has said his children would have to earn the top job, and a jump from senior director to CEO would be a hard sell to shareholders already rattled by this week.Nico Caprez, Huang’s son-in-law, has become the family's power brokerCaprez, 35, is a former Swiss national team ski racer who studied banking and finance at the University of Zurich and worked as a consultant at BCG before meeting Madison as a classmate at London Business School. He joined Nvidia in early 2024 as a corporate development manager, recruited with her help, and became vice president of global AI infrastructure growth in January. The two married in Hawaii in September.The Information, which spoke to more than a dozen people who work with him, described Caprez as Huang's "consigliere" and the company's main contact for neoclouds, the newer cloud providers that rent out Nvidia GPUs. Brookfield's Sikander Rashid has recalled Huang telling him that if he wanted something done, he should talk to Nico. One colleague told the publication they imagined Huang was preparing Madison and Caprez for the next step. Less than three years at the company, though, would make his case harder to defend than anyone else's here.Nvidia's most likely move is Kress now and a longer search after Patrick Moorhead of Moor Insights & Strategy has compared the moment to Intel's 2018 removal of Brian Krzanich over a relationship with an employee, while noting that the chip plans are set years ahead, so the near-term risk to the business is limited. D.A. Davidson's Gil Luria was blunter, warning that the episode could force a transition the company is not prepared for. Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney went the other way, saying that removing Huang would be as foolish as Apple's firing of Steve Jobs.If the board does move, the first name announced is most likely to be Kress. Reports that directors favour her as interim CEO, her 13 years as the company's public financial voice and the board's need to steady investors all point the same way. The permanent job will take a longer search, and on current signals Buck is the insider best placed for it, possibly after a spell sharing the interim role with Kress. Huang always argued that Nvidia did not need a formal succession plan because everyone around him had seen how he thinks. The board is about to find out whether he was right.Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? Find out in the TOI AI Masterclass.

articles.title: A 15-year-old Canadian hockey player facing treatment for a rare cancer has received community support, with a $50,000 fundraising target reached as his family seeks specialist care in the US
articles.summary: Hockey has been a sport of determination, resilience and never giving up. For 15-year-old Alex Bonitatibus it has been no different.
articles.body: Hockey has been a sport of determination, resilience and never giving up. For 15-year-old Alex Bonitatibus it has been no different. But now, the young Canadian is dealing with the biggest challenge of his life after being diagnosed with a rare and aggressive form of cancer. As he embarks on a challenging treatment journey, his local hockey community and supporters have come together to help his family reach an initial fundraising goal of $50,000 to access specialized medical care in the United States.A rare and aggressive cancer diagnosisAccording to a news report by Oakville News, Bonitatibus, a former Oakville Ranger now with the Mississauga Terriers, has been diagnosed with parameningeal rhabdomyosarcoma. The rare cancer forms in the soft tissue and muscle around the sinus area and can be particularly difficult to treat because of its location.The close proximity of the tumor to the brain, eye and critical pathways of the central nervous system makes the conventional surgical intervention extremely difficult. Therefore his treatment requires a highly specialized multidisciplinary oncology team capable of delivering precise and specific therapies, explains the online report.The complexity of the diagnosis has meant that Alex and his family have made it a priority to access advanced medical expertise. Now they are turning to the United States for specialized treatment options that are not available in Canada at this time.A determined young playerOff the back of his diagnosis, Alex is described by teammates and friends as a lively teenager with a great love for hockey. His determination has not only defined his path through the sport, but has also made him a valuable member of his teams, explains Oakville News report.He brings a never-give-up attitude to every game, always giving his best effort no matter what the score is, says Oakville News. His commitment to his teammates and his competitive spirit has built strong ties in the local hockey community.His interests go well beyond the ice. The teenager recently learned how to be a barber and has become sort of an unofficial stylist for his teammates, giving his friends haircuts on a regular basis, adds the report. The hobby is proof of his willingness to learn new skills, and to bring people together, the report adds further.Alex gets support from the communityWith a diagnosis that comes with great medical and financial challenges, Alex’s family has reached out to the wider community for support. A GoFundMe campaign was created to help support these costs, with its original goal set at $50,000. The campaign has been successful in meeting its objective and the response has been encouraging.According to Oakville News, contributions have come from people who know Alex personally, members of the hockey community and other supporters touched by his situation. An anonymous $5,000 donation provided a big boost to the fundraising effort.The road aheadWhile reaching the fundraising goal is a huge milestone, Alex and his family have an uncertain medical journey ahead. As they prepare for the next stage, access to specialist treatment, ongoing care and the expenses related to traveling abroad are the central concerns.The outpouring of support from the community has shown the support the young hockey player has in a very difficult time. For Alex, whose time on the ice has always been defined by perseverance, the support of teammates, friends and well-wishers is an important source of strength as he faces his toughest challenge yet.Images Courtesy: istockYou use AI every day. articles.title: Daniel Thomas admits criminal damage of boat in English Channel
articles.summary: Activist Danny Tommo pleads guilty to criminal damage at Portsmouth Crown Court.
articles.body:
Anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas, also known as Danny Tommo, has admitted criminal damage after slashing a dinghy with a knife in the English Channel.

The 37-year-old changed his plea to the single charge when he appeared via video link from prison at Portsmouth Crown Court on Thursday.

A court previously heard he had taken a boat into the English Channel on 22 September and observed the migrant occupants of a dinghy being assisted by the RNLI, Border Force and the French Coastguard.

Thomas admitted using a knife on the dinghy, which had French personnel on board.

Prosecutor Kevin Lucie told Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in September the defendant instructed his vessel to be steered towards the empty rigid inflatable boat (RIB) that was adrift.

The court heard he then armed himself with a knife as rescue crews also approached the dinghy and a Frenchman boarded from a rescue vessel.

After slashing the boat with the knife, Thomas could be heard on a livestream saying: "This is what needs to happen to everyone in these boats.

"Right, you're on English territory, This is England, this is not France anymore.

"Get off the boat, you have time to get off the boat. This is not France. Take them back."

More stories from Hampshire & the Isle of Wight

Listen to the latest news from Hampshire and the Isle of Wight

After he pleaded guilty to the charge of criminal damage, he reiterated his plea of not guilty to failing to disclose the pin to his phone to police.

Thomas, whose address was withheld by the court at a previous hearing, will be sentenced at the same court on 18 November.

The maximum sentence if convicted of criminal damage valued at more than £5,000 is 10 years' imprisonment, according to the Sentencing Council.

But if the damage is valued lower than £5,000, the maximum sentence could be a fine and three months' jail time.

Thomas will also be given credit for his guilty plea.

articles.title: Joe Torre grew up in a home marked by violence; the charity he founded with wife Ali now runs 30 school support sites, offering counselling and safe spaces for children affected by abuse and trauma
articles.summary: Children who experience violence at home may find it difficult to speak about what is happening to them.
articles.body: Children who experience violence at home may find it difficult to speak about what is happening to them. Some may also believe they are responsible for the problems within their families. A foundation started by former New York Yankees manager Joe Torre and his wife, Ali, aims to help such children find support within their schools.The Joe Torre Safe At Home Foundation now operates 30 school-based support centres under its Margaret's Place programme. The centres provide counselling and safe spaces for students affected by domestic violence, abuse and trauma. The foundation says it reached more than 49,000 children during the current year.According the organisation's webiste, it has directly served more than 275,000 young people, their families, schools and communities since it was established in 2002. Its work is based on the belief that children should have access to trusted adults and a safe environment where they can discuss difficult experiences.For Torre, the initiative has a personal connection. He grew up in a household where his father abused his mother, Margaret. The experience affected his childhood and continued to influence how he viewed himself during his professional baseball career.He and Ali established Safe At Home to address domestic violence and abuse through education. The foundation's school programme was named Margaret's Place in honour of his mother. It was designed to give children access to the kind of support that can be difficult to find when violence is taking place within their homes.Schools provide safe place to seek helpMargaret's Place operates through dedicated rooms inside schools. Students can visit these spaces to talk to someone or spend time in an environment where they feel comfortable. The foundation says respect and confidentiality are central to how these rooms function.The programme offers individual and group counselling to students affected by violence and trauma. It also gives them an opportunity to connect with others who may have faced similar situations.The aim is to make it easier for children to seek help rather than keep their experiences to themselves. Students can speak about their concerns without feeling that they have to deal with everything alone.The foundation also tracks how students respond to the support they receive. Its reported figures show that 94% of students said they felt safer after receiving help through the programme.Another 88% said talking to someone had become easier than keeping their feelings to themselves. The organisation also reported that 91% of students felt more confident and had better self-esteem. In addition, 95% said they were more hopeful about their future.These figures are part of the foundation's reported impact assessment. They reflect the changes students said they experienced through the programme.Torre's childhood shaped foundation's missionTorre's decision to work on domestic violence was connected to what he witnessed while growing up in Brooklyn, New York. He was the youngest of five children. His father, who worked as a New York Police Department officer, abused his mother.Although Torre went on to build a successful baseball career, he said his experiences at home affected his confidence and how he dealt with setbacks.In an interview published by Major League Baseball in 2019, Torre spoke about feeling responsible when his team lost games. He often believed there was something more he could have done to prevent a defeat.He also recalled how difficult it was to understand the violence in his home as a child. His mother did not discuss the abuse with him, even though he could see its effects.“I felt like I was responsible for what was going on, because there was a lot of whispering going on in my house, and my mom would never share it with me, even though I saw the results of what my dad did to her,” Torre said.He did not speak publicly about his childhood experiences for many years. He later understood that the feelings of guilt and low self-esteem he carried were connected to what had happened at home.His experience also influenced the message he wanted the foundation to communicate to children facing similar circumstances.“The most important thing that they realize is that they’re not alone and it’s not their fault,” Torre said while discussing the programme.He explained that the support offered through Margaret's Place was not a cure for violence at home. Children would still have to return to their families and deal with their circumstances. However, the programme could give them tools to handle those situations and help build their confidence and self-respect.Programme has expanded since its launchWhen MLB reported on the foundation in August 2019, it had 15 Margaret's Place programmes in four US states. Nearly 100,000 students had been connected with resources through its work at that time.The organisation now lists 30 school programme sites across New York City, Westchester, Los Angeles, Cincinnati and Tahiti. These locations serve students from kindergarten through Class 12.The foundation's work also involves families and school communities. Its stated mission is to prevent domestic violence and abuse through education and provide support to young people affected by trauma.Safe At Home is continuing its fundraising efforts to maintain and expand these services. Ali and Joe Torre are scheduled to host the foundation's 2026 Annual New York Gala on November 12 at Gotham Hall in New York City.The event will honour Darrell and Beth Rigel for their support of the organisation. Proceeds are expected to help sustain its programmes in New York and other locations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A rare 24-carat Bulgari Pink diamond that had remained with the same family since the 1950s has sold for more than $14.6 million at Christie's in Geneva, decades after its original purchase
articles.summary: A rare 24-carat pink diamond, known as the Bulgari Pink, has sold for more than $14.6 million at a Christie’s jewellery auction in Geneva.
articles.body: A rare 24-carat pink diamond, known as the Bulgari Pink, has sold for more than $14.6 million at a Christie’s jewellery auction in Geneva. The emerald-cut stone, which had remained in the same family since it was purchased in the 1950s, fetched 12.1 million Swiss francs at auction, placing it squarely within the pre-sale estimate of 10 to 15 million Swiss francs. The sale has drawn attention not only because of the price, but because of the diamond’s remarkable provenance. Believed to have originated from the legendary Golconda mines in India, the Bulgari Pink carries a history that stretches back decades and connects one of the world’s most celebrated jewellery houses with one of the most storied sources of diamonds in history, as per the Associated Press (AP). Read more details about it here:A diamond with a long family historyThe Bulgari Pink was purchased by a family in the 1950s and has remained with them ever since. That kind of unbroken ownership is increasingly rare in the high-end jewellery market, where many significant stones change hands multiple times over the decades.The fact that the diamond stayed within one family for so long adds a layer of intimacy to its story. It was not simply an investment asset or a museum piece. It was a jewel that lived within a household, passed through generations and carried personal meaning alongside its extraordinary monetary value.When such a stone finally comes to market, it often attracts attention from collectors, investors and institutions alike. In this case, the Bulgari Pink was positioned as the headline lot of Christie’s seasonal jewellery sale in Geneva, a clear sign of how highly the auction house regarded it.Why the Bulgari Pink mattersThe Bulgari Pink is a 24-carat fancy intense pink diamond, a classification that places it among the most sought-after coloured diamonds in the world. Pink diamonds are exceptionally rare, and stones of this size and intensity are even rarer still.The emerald cut gives the diamond a clean, architectural appearance that allows the colour to take centre stage. Rather than relying on brilliance alone, the cut emphasises clarity, symmetry and the depth of the pink hue, qualities that collectors prize highly.Plus there's that Bulgari association to add weight.Bulgari is an Italian jewelry house that stands for bold design and exceptional craftsmanship. A diamond set by Bulgari has a level of recognition that goes beyond the stone.The Golconda linkThe Bulgari Pink’s supposed connection to the Golconda mines of southern India makes it all the more compelling. These mines have produced some of the most famous diamonds in history, including the Koh-i-Noor and the Hope Diamond.Golconda diamonds are sought after not only for their beauty but for their historical significance.The region has a long history with extraordinary stones and diamonds from these mines are often said to have a pedigree beyond normal provenance.For collectors, the idea that the Bulgari Pink may have originated from Golconda adds a layer of romance and rarity. It links the stone to a lineage of legendary diamonds that have shaped the history of luxury and wealth.A sale within expectationsAhead of the auction, Christie’s estimated that the Bulgari Pink would fetch between 10 and 15 million Swiss francs, or roughly 12 to 18 million US dollars. The final hammer price of 12.1 million Swiss francs, or more than 14.6 million US dollars, landed comfortably within that range.The result suggests that the market for exceptional coloured diamonds remains strong, even as broader luxury markets fluctuate. Stones with rare colour, significant size and clear provenance continue to command serious attention from buyers around the world.Christie’s global head of jewellery, Max Fawcett, described the Bulgari Pink as the Mona Lisa of pink diamonds ahead of the sale. That kind of language reflects not just marketing, but a genuine recognition of how unusual the stone is.A broader jewellery saleThe Bulgari Pink was not the only significant item in the Geneva auction. Christie’s also offered a private collection of nearly 300 twentieth-century jewels, including pieces from Bulgari, Cartier and Graff.The inclusion of such a wide range of houses and styles gave the sale a broader appeal, drawing interest from collectors with different tastes and budgets. Still, it was the Bulgari Pink that stood out as the centrepiece of the event.The sale highlights how the jewellery market continues to evolve. While classic names like Bulgari, Cartier and Graff remain central, the real drivers of value are often rarity, history and the story behind a particular stone.What the sale says about the marketThe strong result for the Bulgari Pink suggests that top-tier coloured diamonds are still seen as a store of value, even in uncertain economic times. Buyers continue to seek out stones that combine rarity with provenance and brand recognition.The diamond’s appeal was probably enhanced by the fact it had remained in one family for decades. Provenance has become increasingly important in the luxury market, and a clear ownership history can significantly enhance a jewel’s desirability.For the family that sold it, the sale marks the end of a long chapter. For the purchaser it is the beginning of a new one. Either way, the Bulgari Pink has proven once again that great diamonds are more than beautiful objects. They are pieces of history that continue to command attention, admiration and extraordinary prices.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Resident Evil Requiem sweeps Golden Joystick Awards
articles.summary: The latest instalment in the franchise, which is marking 30 years, bagged the top prize.
articles.body:
Resident Evil Requiem and its makers have won big at the Golden Joystick Awards, which celebrate the year's most popular games.

Released in February, it was the latest instalment of the global survival horror phenomenon, which has also spawned books, films and TV programmes since it was first released 30 years ago.

At Wednesday's awards ceremony, it scooped ultimate game of the year, console game of the year, best game trailer, and best lead performer for the game's star Angela Sant'Albano, who plays protagonist Grace Ashcroft.

Meanwhile its makers, Japanese studio Capcom, was named studio of the year and was also recognised for other games, including Onimusha: Way of the Sword and Pragmata.

FBI agent Grace Ashcroft was a brand new lead character in Resident Evil Requiem who, along with returning fan favourite Leon S. Kennedy, explores old haunts, such as Racoon City's police department as they investigate a series of mysterious deaths.

Securing 17% of the public vote, it was named ultimate game of the year ahead of other contenders Phantom Blade Zero, Crimson Desert, Control Resonant and The Blood of Dawnwalker.

There were prizes across 25 categories up for grabs - 22 of which are decided by a public vote amongst gamers from around the world.

While streamers' choice, critics' choice and developers' choice award are decided by critics.

Two of those went to indie hit Meccha Chameleon, a multiplayer hide-and-seek game where players paint themselves to blend in with their surroundings to evade others playing as hunters.

As well as streamers' choice and developers' choice, it also bagged best multiplayer game and best indie game - self published, which were chosen by the public.

Big Walk - a co-operative online game produced by Australian developer House House - was named critics' choice winner.

The studio was criticised this week after reports it used generative AI in the final stretch of the game's development - something it did not disclose at the time of the its release.

It said the tool was used to produce a tiny amount of code.

Best Multiplayer Game - Meccha Chameleon

Best Game Expansion - Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations

articles.title: Stewardess Violet Jessop was aboard the RMS Olympic when it collided with a warship in 1911, survived the Titanic sinking in 1912, and then survived the sinking of its sister ship Britannic in 1916
articles.summary: Violet Jessop's life at sea was marked by three disasters involving some of the most famous ships in maritime history.
articles.body: Violet Jessop's life at sea was marked by three disasters involving some of the most famous ships in maritime history. The Argentine-born stewardess survived the 1911 collision involving the RMS Olympic, the sinking of the RMS Titanic in 1912 and the loss of the HMHS Britannic during World War I in 1916. Her remarkable experiences earned her the nickname 'Miss Unsinkable'. According to her memoir Titanic Survivor, published with biographer John Maxtone-Graham, and historical accounts from Biography dot com and Encyclopedia Titanica, Jessop was not merely a passenger caught up in these events. She was a working member of the crews who witnessed the disasters at close quarters and continued her career at sea afterwards.From Argentina to a career at seaBorn in Argentina in 1887 to Irish parents, Jessop was the eldest of a large family. Her childhood was marked by serious illness, including tuberculosis, which she survived despite doctors reportedly believing she would not recover. Following her father's death, the family moved to England. Her mother subsequently found work as a ship stewardess, but when she became ill, Jessop left school to help support the family. She eventually followed the same profession, beginning her career aboard the Royal Mail Line's Orinoco in 1908. Her work brought her into contact with the rapidly expanding transatlantic shipping industry, where ocean liners were increasingly associated with luxury, speed and international travel. In 1911, she joined the White Star Line and began working aboard the RMS Olympic.The first disaster aboard OlympicJessop's first major encounter with a maritime disaster came on September 20, 1911. She was working aboard the Olympic when the liner collided with HMS Hawke, a British Royal Navy warship, in the Solent near the Isle of Wight.The collision seriously damaged the Olympic, including a large section of its hull. However, the ship managed to return to port without assistance, and no lives were lost. The incident did not end Jessop's career with White Star Line. After the Olympic returned for repairs, she continued working for the company. In April 1912, she was transferred to its newer sister ship, the Titanic, which was preparing for its maiden voyage.Surviving the Titanic sinkingJessop boarded the Titanic in Southampton on April 10, 1912, as a first-class stewardess. Four days later, on April 14, the ship struck an iceberg in the North Atlantic. It sank in the early hours of April 15, killing more than 1,500 people. As the disaster unfolded, Jessop was instructed to go on deck and help demonstrate how passengers should behave during the evacuation. She watched crew members prepare the lifeboats before being ordered into lifeboat 16.During the evacuation, an officer handed her a baby to hold. She later recalled that the child's mother took the infant back after the survivors reached the rescue ship, RMS Carpathia. Jessop and the other survivors were eventually brought to New York. Despite the trauma of the sinking, she returned to Southampton and continued working at sea.A third encounter with disaster aboard BritannicWhen World War I broke out in 1914, Jessop volunteered for nursing duties with the British Red Cross and served with the Voluntary Aid Detachment. She was eventually assigned to the HMHS Britannic, the third Olympic-class liner, which had been converted into a hospital ship. On November 21, 1916, while travelling through the Aegean Sea, the Britannic struck a German naval mine. The explosion caused severe damage, and the ship began taking in water rapidly.The evacuation soon turned dangerous. As the vessel listed, some lifeboats were drawn towards its still-turning propellers. Jessop was among those caught in the danger and jumped into the water to escape. She was pulled beneath the ship's keel and struck her head, sustaining an injury that she later discovered had caused a skull fracture. The Britannic sank in approximately 55 minutes. Of the 1,066 people aboard, 30 died. Jessop survived once again, although the experience left her with a serious head injury.Life after three maritime disastersRemarkably, Jessop did not abandon her profession after surviving three separate maritime incidents. She returned to work for the White Star Line in 1920 and subsequently joined the Red Star Line before returning to the Royal Mail Line. During her career, she travelled extensively, including two voyages around the world aboard the Red Star Line's Belgenland. She eventually retired in 1950 and settled in Great Ashfield, Suffolk, England.Jessop died on May 5, 1971, aged 83, from congestive heart failure. Her extraordinary experiences continued to attract attention long after her retirement, and she became widely known as 'Miss Unsinkable'. Her story remains an unusual chapter in maritime history, not simply because she survived two major shipwrecks, but because she continued working at sea after witnessing disasters that claimed so many lives.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'I would’ve not gone forward': Biden says he would have dropped out of 2024 race if he knew about cancer
articles.summary: In a candid interview, former President Joe Biden reveals he would have reconsidered a second term had he known about his cancer diagnosis, while downplaying the impact of his criticized 2024 debate performance against Trump.
articles.body: Former US president Joe Biden has said he would not have pursued a second term in the White House if he had known he was suffering from cancer, while also dismissing the impact of his widely criticised 2024 debate performance against Donald Trump.In an interview with PEOPLE, Biden said he felt unwell before his prostate cancer diagnosis but did not know the illness was responsible. He was diagnosed with an aggressive form of the disease in May 2025, four months after leaving office.“If I had known that I was feeling lousy because I had cancer, I would have resigned. I would’ve not gone forward, because I don’t think an 80-year-old man with cancer should be running for (president),” Biden said.He added that he believed he was the person best equipped to serve as president at the time, saying: “I believe that on an objective basis, I was the best-equipped person to do the job.”Biden also rejected suggestions that he had concealed information about his health while in office. He said the public was informed after his diagnosis was confirmed.“I didn’t do that. We let the public know when I found out, when I knew what was going on,” he told PEOPLE, adding that national leaders should be open about health conditions that affect them.The interview comes ahead of the release of Biden’s presidential memoir, Promise Me, America, scheduled for next Tuesday. The former president has said his cancer diagnosis will limit his ability to promote the book.Biden plays down impact of 2024 debateBiden also addressed his June 2024 debate against Trump, which intensified concerns about his ability to continue as the Democratic presidential candidate. During the televised encounter, he appeared confused at several points and struggled to articulate his arguments, triggering calls within his party for him to reconsider his candidacy.However, Biden described the debate as having little influence on his decision to leave the race.“Look, I don’t know anybody who hasn’t made a mistake in a debate,” he said. “To me, it was not very consequential.”He said he had expected another debate to take place and maintained that the absence of a second encounter did not change his assessment of the first.Biden eventually withdrew from the presidential contest and endorsed then-vice president Kamala Harris, just 107 days before the November 2024 election. A second debate took place in September, with Harris facing Trump.The performance also raised concerns within Biden's family. articles.title: Why the UK economy is surprisingly resilient
articles.summary: The UK is seeing impressive growth, but will it last?
articles.body:
The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September.

"Top gear" and "strikingly strong" were among the descriptions of the 0.7% growth offered by the economists who track every minor murmur of Britain's economy.

It is an upgrade on "solid" and "resilient", and in turn a world away from "hardest hit by the Iran War".

Against the backdrop of the world's biggest disruption to energy flows, rising market borrowing costs - and the cruel summers since the pandemic - it is impressive growth.

It should reset some of the swirl of self-reinforcing negativity.

The UK's economic growth has averaged less than 0.1% in the four Q3s [ie July to September] since the pandemic.

The average prediction just months ago for this July to September was just 0.1%.

Even the UK's official forecaster the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) effectively pencilled in 0.3% at the Budget just 3 weeks ago.

This figure has not been exceeded outside the pandemic since 2017. It puts the UK on course to be the second fastest growing economy after the US across the major G7 countries which also includes Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France.

It is tempting to think about what the economy would have done if the Iran War hadn't happened. If interest rates had been cut instead of their recent rise.

While the latest figure kills the doom, it is clearly not a boom either.

Spending on AI and tech have driven the surprise upside over the year. While the AI data centre boom may at any point turn to bust, these figures suggest that spending across the economy on investing in these technologies is helping to boost growth. Consumers have been resilient, at least till the autumn, perhaps helped by better economic vibes.

While there has been an understandable focus on high UK borrowing costs, another measure of the international standing of the UK economy, sterling's value, reached post Brexit referendum highs last week.

Productivity and investment is also looking stronger, especially after recent revisions. Some of the most encouraging figures are in private sector business investment.

I spoke to the chancellor at Nexeon in Oxfordshire, which is searching for a UK factory to manufacture its cutting edge electric vehicle battery - and British - technology. My colleagues visited British watchmakers in Maidenhead carving out a niche to take on the Swiss.

However, this may well not last for the final three months of the year.

Consumer confidence has already fallen as petrol and domestic energy prices start to rise again.

There is a significant challenge with everyday cost-of-living pressures in the coming months. Construction and private house building remain depressed.

The Iran conflict remains the big unknown and whether post the US midterm elections there could be a durable end to the conflict in the Gulf.

Some oil and gas production there is starting to normalise. It could bring down petrol prices, energy bills, government borrowing costs, and mortgage costs too.

Expect to see Downing Street investing heavily in "settlement of the conflict", which the chancellor told me is the "best economic policy".

articles.title: The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal
articles.summary: Within days, Huang's status as a seemingly untouchable figure leading the global tech race has crumbled.
articles.body:
Jensen Huang, known for sporting a black leather jacket to shareholder events, appeared to have it all. He was courted by leaders in both Washington and Beijing, worshipped by investors and seen as a loyal family man. But a rockstar approach to his personal life has ultimately led to his resignation.

The 63-year-old has been married since 1985, long before the foundation of Nvidia, the company that propelled him to tech stardom.

He is known as a workaholic and a demanding manager, with high standards for those who worked for him, which included his own children, promoted within the company. But he has seen his personal reputation go into free fall this week, undone by romantic entanglements, that throw doubt on his focus and his judgement.

On Thursday he resigned following back-to-back revelations of two affairs. News of the first - a relationship with a businesswoman, alleged to be a Chinese spy - ricocheted around the world, raising eyebrows among investors. It was followed on Wednesday by reports that the tech boss had also had an affair with an Nvidia colleague.

His departure creates uncertainty in the global stock market, which was already knocked-off balance in recent weeks. Nvidia is a linchpin in the US's race for technology leadership with China.

Huang may not be a household name on the same level as Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg.

But his role in the tech industry, especially in relation to the explosion of artificial intelligence in the last three years, may prove more consequential. Nvidia dominates the market for the microchips that are used to power the new technology.

The company, which is still valued at nearly $4 trillion despite recent events, is at the centre of the AI race between the US and China, the world's tech and economic powerhouses.

Huang enjoyed access to the seats of political power on an unrivalled scale, being courted by both US President Donald Trump and China's President XI Jinping.

His remarkable rise to the top of his profession has led to him being dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech" and seen him amass an estimated fortune of $145bn (£109bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

Despite always donning his trademark all-black outfits and taking a playful approach to investor presentations, Huang has worked for years to present himself as a family man, someone who exemplified the American Dream.

Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang and his family moved to the west coast of the US when he was nine years old. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University.

It was at college where he met his wife, Lori Mills. The pair were lab partners and married in 1985, eight years before Huang founded Nvidia.

They have two children, Madison and Spencer, who now both work in senior roles at their father's firm.

The company became a key provider of the computer chips and circuits used for gaming before it expanded in a new direction. It now creates the key processing chips used to power the growing AI technology.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after tech giant rocked by second affair allegation

Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia's chief executive?

Huang has hailed AI as a "new industrial revolution" that is on par with the advent of electricity. Nvidia is the world's second most valuable company and its customers include the biggest firms on the planet, Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, SpaceX, Tesla, OpenAI and Anthropic, all spending big on its products.

So it is no surprise that at a recent AI summit at the White House, Huang was picked out from a group of 42 to flank the president, alongside Elon Musk, both men with whom Trump has famously close relationships.

"Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on Jensen Huang, told the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today.

He described Huang as a "demanding" boss, who "really pushes his people to the limit".

While he says Huang is "very brilliant" and a "world-class computer scientist", there's also "a level of arrogance" and "a level of self-deception as well", he said.

Huang had gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, he added, something that was "very important to him".

"He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," Witt added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad."

First reports emerged on 29 October in the New York Times that Huang had conducted a relationship with Alice Huang, no relation. US officials allege the businesswoman associated with Singapore-based firm Megaspeed, is a Chinese intelligence asset.

After the revelations of the first affair, Huang admitted to having been "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting their family.

Trump, as well as other leaders in the AI tech industry, initially backed Huang to continue in his role at Nvidia. The president described him as "honourable".

But the reporting of a second affair, with Kimberly Powell, vice president of healthcare who has worked at Nvidia for 18 years, prompted a board meeting, followed by the announcement Huang was stepping down.

In the aftermath of that news Trump said Huang had done "a fantastic job" and proposed Tim Cook of Apple as a suitable replacement at the head of Nvidia.

articles.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO: Who takes over, what lies ahead, and why the trouble isn’t over for Huang and Nvidia
articles.summary: Nvidia went 33 years without ever having to say who would follow Jensen Huang.
articles.body: Nvidia went 33 years without ever having to say who would follow Jensen Huang. That is now the company's most urgent question, and it has to be answered with the share price falling and the world watching. Colette Kress is minding the shop as interim CEO while directors look for a permanent chief. Investigators in Washington are still digging, and the push to sell American AI chips to China has lost the executive who argued for it hardest.The board removed the preeminent face of the AI infrastructure boom after reports of two affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China. Huang fought to keep his job, The New York Times reported, but plans for Kress to step in were already in motion by Wednesday.Nvidia shares tumbled a little more than 14% after the opening bell to $148.80, their lowest price since June 2025. The stock has since clawed back some ground and was trading at about $166.30, down roughly 7% for the day, at the time of writingColette Kress is interim CEO, so who runs Nvidia next and why Jensen Huang is hard to replaceKress was always meant to be a bridge. She will run the company and its finances at the same time, and the search for a permanent chief is open to outsiders as well as insiders. Directors had been working with an outside firm to identify potential replacements even before the announcement, a sign the board had planned for this outcome.A shortlist has already taken shape. Analysts and investors keep coming back to two internal names: Kress and Ian Buck, the engineer who runs product for hyperscale AI. Outside names include Arm chief Rene Haas, who previously worked at Nvidia, and Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji. Jeff Fisher, a 32-year Nvidia veteran, has also come up. Minotaur Capital's Armina Rosenberg has suggested a split arrangement, with a finance-minded leader such as Kress sharing the top job with a technologist such as Buck.The difficulty is less about names than about how Nvidia was built. Huang has said he is opposed to succession planning. He managed more than 60 direct reports, a flat setup that will be hard to unwind. He once said traditional org charts made no sense to him, and he claimed to read several thousand emails a day. His Santa Clara office is built around an enormous oval desk facing his lieutenants, with stadium seating behind them.Money is tied to his name too. Nvidia sits on about $99 billion in equity investments, spread across frontier AI labs, neoclouds and infrastructure firms. In August, it lined up more than $500 billion in data centre financing with six large financial institutions. Morningstar's Brian Colello wrote this week that it is unclear what those arrangements look like under another CEO, and that borrowing could get costlier without Huang orchestrating them. Futurum Equities' Shay Boloor framed the long-term risk around vision: Huang has been the person who consistently identified where computing is going.Alice Huang spy investigation, FBI and Congress: Jensen Huang's troubles are not overLeaving Nvidia does not take Huang out of the line of fire. The board's own inquiry, run with the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen and Katz, has an uncertain future now that its subject has gone. The federal investigations are wider. The Justice Department is running several probes that touch on Alice Huang, The Wall Street Journal reported, and Trump said on Monday that the FBI was examining the relationship.New detail has emerged on how long Washington knew. According to the Times, a classified memo overseen by Secretary of State Marco Rubio circulated among officials before Trump's China trip in May, warning that the Megaspeed executive was allegedly working for China's Ministry of State Security. Trump had also reportedly been briefed about her roughly a year ago and chose not to act.Then there is the money trail. Megaspeed's sister company in Malaysia spent $4.8 billion or more on Nvidia chips and technology between June 2024 and February 2026, according to trade records cited by the Times. That is an unusually large bill for a small firm, at a time when Nvidia hardware is rationed. Both companies deny wrongdoing, and Beijing has dismissed the claims as "nothing but smears."Capitol Hill is next in line. In a November 4 letter, the Republican chairs of three House committees asked Huang to a closed-door briefing on November 18. They want to know about his dealings with Alice Huang and whether Beijing shaped Nvidia's decisions or US chip export policy. Lawmakers have also raised the threat of a subpoena.The board's ability to act was never in doubt. Nvidia has one class of stock with one vote per share, and independent directors hold 10 of its 11 seats. Unlike the founders of Meta or Alphabet, Huang had no super-voting shares to protect his job.What Jensen Huang's exit means for US chip export controls, China and the AI boomThe biggest effects may show up in policy. Huang was corporate America's leading advocate of selling to China, and in 2025 he called US export curbs "a failure." His pitch was that American chips in Chinese data centres would make US technology the global standard. In July 2025, he made that case to Trump in the Oval Office, and days later H20 sales to China were cleared. By December, Trump allowed sales to approved Chinese buyers, with the US government taking a 25% cut.The lobbying and the scandal are separate things. CSET analyst Hanna Dohmen has noted that Nvidia had every commercial reason to push for looser rules, intelligence operation or not, since each restriction caps its sales. The affair has still damaged the messenger. A trio of bills to restrict chip sales abroad has gained momentum. One of them, already passed by the House and awaiting the Senate, would extend controls to cloud computing, stopping Chinese firms from renting advanced Nvidia servers in countries such as Malaysia. Chinese AI stocks fell on Thursday on fears that their access to top-end chips could narrow.The White House has not turned on him. Trump called Huang "an honorable guy" and said he had "done an amazing job for our country." Huang's financial grip on Nvidia also remains large even without a board seat. More than half of his 922 million shares sit in a trust he co-manages with his wife, Lori. Elon Musk has said he would be open to hiring him.Nvidia stock and Q3 earnings: What investors will watch on November 17Kress faces her first public test within a week. Nvidia reports third-quarter fiscal 2027 results on November 17, with the earnings call at 2 pm PT, or 3:30 am IST on November 18. She has sat beside Huang on these calls for years. On this one, analysts will spend as much time on leadership as on data centre revenue.The sell side moved before the board did. As reports of Huang's likely removal surfaced on Wednesday night, Bernstein downgraded the stock and halved its target from $400 to $200. Oppenheimer dropped its target entirely and warned of a possible "brain drain," and Evercore cut its target to $186 from $330. Earlier in the week, tech analyst Dan Ives had already put a number on the Huang premium: $300 a share with him, $225 without. Estimates are that the slide could erase roughly $1 trillion from Nvidia's market value this month alone.There is a bull case, and it rests on the product pipeline. Blackwell demand, the Rubin roadmap, networking and the CUDA software ecosystem were all locked in before the scandal, which is why some analysts want the leadership crisis kept apart from the business.The board has promised continuity. Whether Nvidia's customers, lenders and engineers believe it will become clearer on November 17, when a company that has spoken in Huang's voice since 1993 reports for the first time without him.Your child uses AI every day. articles.title: Indians top list again: 9.25 lakh acquired citizenship of OECD countries over past five years
articles.summary: Indians continue to top the list of people acquiring citizenship in advanced economies, with around 9.25 lakh Indian citizens acquiring the nationality of
articles.body: Indians continue to top the list of people acquiring citizenship in advanced economies, with around 9.25 lakh Indian citizens acquiring the nationality of an OECD member country between 2020 and 2024, according to the ‘International Migration Outlook – 2026’ report released on Thursday by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).The figure marks a sharp increase of 41% from just over 6.5 lakh Indians who acquired citizenship of OECD member countries during 2015–2019. India remains the largest country of former nationality among those acquiring citizenship in OECD member countries, ahead of Syria and Mexico, whose nationals accounted for around 5.9 lakh citizenships in these countries each during the five-year period 2020–2024. Interestingly, while China was the sixth largest source country whose nationals acquired OECD member country citizenship, the numbers fell by nearly 12% to 3.4 lakh in 2020-2024 as compared to the previous five-year period.OECD comprises 38 member countries – notably US, UK, European nations, Australia, Canada, Japan and South Korea.According to additional data shared with TOI, during the five-year period 2020-2024, OECD member countries embraced nearly 87 lakh new citizens – Indians constitute around 10% of its new citizens. In the previous five-year period, nearly 65 lakh individuals acquired citizenship of an OECD member country – once again the composition of Indians was 10%.Acquisitions of citizenship in OECD countries by former nationalityCountry of former nationality2015–20192020–2024(% increase/decrease)India6,54,8219,25,737 (+41.4%)Mexico6,09,1155,90,248 (-3.1%)Syria98,4635,88,219 (+497.4%)Morocco4,24,5385,07,951 (+19.6%)Philippines4,33,6025,03,679 (+16.2%)China3,89,3163,42,808 (-11.9%)OECD also shared year-on-year India-specific data with TOI, showing that 2.30 lakh Indians acquired citizenship of OECD member countries in 2024, mainly in Canada (87,320), the US (48,820) and Australia (28,969). In 2023, the overall India-figure was marginally lower at nearly 2.25 lakh, with the same three countries accounting for most of the citizenship acquisitions.The report attributes the increase in Indian citizenship in OECD member countries to the growth of Indian communities in several member countries, particularly Canada. A total of 2.61 lakh Indians became Canadian citizens during 2020–2024, an increase of 150% compared with the preceding five-year period. The numbers were also high in the US, the UK and Australia.The latest figures underline the growing permanence of Indian migration to advanced economies. While immigration flows measure the number of people moving to another country, citizenship acquisitions offer an indication of how many immigrants have progressed to acquiring the nationality of their destination country.Leading OECD-countries where Indians acquiring citizenshipOECD countryIndians acquiring citizenship in 2023Indians acquiring citizenship in 2024Canada78,48787,320United States52,36048,820Australia40,36128,969United Kingdom18,31924,888New Zealand6,6095,778Total across OECD countries2,24,6302,30,337The OECD's latest report also records a rise in new citizenships from various nationalities across its member countries. Around 3 million (30 lakh) people acquired the nationality of an OECD country in 2025. The US accounted for almost 9 lakh new citizens – a rise of 9% over 2024, followed by Germany and Spain with 3 lakh new citizens each registering a rise of 9% and 6% over the previous year. Canada ranked only fourth in 2025, due to a 22% drop, and registered nearly 3 lakh new citizens. However, India's strong showing is particularly evident in Canada, which has been a major destination for Indian migrants over the past decade, with established communities contributing to the pool of people eligible to apply for citizenship.Indians also continued to move to OECD member countries for work and study, although the pace of migration slowed. India remained the largest origin country of new migrants to OECD member countries in 2024. However, the number of Indian-origin migrants moving to OECD member countries fell by 19% in 2024, from 6.07 lakh in 2023 to 4.94 lakh in 2024.“Migration remains high, and immigrants now account for 16% of employment across the OECD,” Mathias Cormann, OECD Secretary-General said. “With ageing populations and slower productivity growth, countries cannot afford to waste the skills migrants bring. That means helping migrants move into jobs where they can contribute most, and giving immigrant entrepreneurs better access to finance, networks and business support,” he added.Immigrants accounted for 12% of the OECD member countries population in 2025, up from 9% in 2015. In just over half of OECD countries, immigrants contributed at least 50% of employment growth between 2014 and 2024.Number of Indians acquiring citizenship of an OECD member countryYearNumber of Indians acquiring citizenship20101,33,28020111,13,64020121,05,06720131,34,36420141,29,19020151,27,37420161,29,32320171,21,15120181,21,29920191,55,67420201,32,62120211,32,87720222,05,27220232,24,63020242,30,337One in five STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) graduates across OECD member countries is foreign-born, and immigrants are over-represented among researchers and founders of innovative firms. Yet immigrants are also more likely to work in lower-productivity firms and sectors, with their skills often underutilised, states OECD. The report finds that immigrant’s contribution to productivity depends on how effectively countries make use of their skills and support investment and innovation – many countries have expanded programmes to attract highly skilled workers.International student inflows to OECD member countries fell from 19 lakh in 2024 to 16 lakh in 2025, with the decline concentrated in traditional English-speaking destinations. In contrast, European countries continued to attract growing numbers of international students, especially Austria, Germany and Italy. China and India remained the largest source countries.The gap between Indian and Chinese students studying in OECD member countries narrowed, with 8.3 lakh Indian students and 8.50 lakh Chinese students studying in these countries.With restrictive immigration policies being introduced in several OECD member countries such as the US, UK, Canada and Australia, immigration experts believe that the number of temporary workers and students could show a decline over the next few years. However, it is likely that Indians will continue to top the charts in citizenship acquisition and their foray overseas for work and study.Permanent migration to OECD member countries declined by 1.6% in 2025, falling for the second consecutive year, but remained historically high at nearly 60 lakh new permanent immigrants. Permanent migration covers people moving for family reunification, work or humanitarian reasons with a long term right to stay. With restrictive policies in major destination countries, this has shown a decline.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: A Missouri father argued a $20,000 bankruptcy deal erased $243,780 he owed his ex-wife after their divorce; a November 10 appeals court found $12,969.85 still due and revived a separate child-support dispute
articles.summary: A Missouri man who claimed that a $20,000 bankruptcy settlement had cleared his financial obligations to his former wife has been told that he still owes
articles.body: A Missouri man who claimed that a $20,000 bankruptcy settlement had cleared his financial obligations to his former wife has been told that he still owes $12,969.85. An appeals court has overturned a lower court's decision that he had fulfilled his payment obligations under an earlier contempt judgment.The Missouri Court of Appeals Eastern District delivered the ruling on November 10, in a dispute between Patricia K. Fish and her former husband, Brian D. Fish. The court found that the lower court had wrongly counted payments Brian made before the bankruptcy settlement while calculating what remained unpaid.The dispute dates back to the couple's 2014 divorce. Patricia received sole legal and physical custody of their minor children. Brian was directed to pay monthly child support and contribute towards their medical, dental and educational expenses.The divorce court also made Brian responsible for four civil lawsuits involving allegations that he had forged Patricia's signature on financial documents. The cases carried potential liabilities of at least $1.95 million. He was ordered to protect Patricia from any financial losses arising from them.How the debt reached $243,780Patricia approached the court in 2016, alleging that Brian had failed to pay child support and his share of the children's expenses. She also accused him of violating their parenting plan and failing to protect her from the civil lawsuits. She said she had spent more than $200,000 defending herself and settling those cases.In November 2017, the trial court found Brian in contempt and calculated that he owed Patricia $243,780. This included $217,756.26 for expenses linked to the civil lawsuits, $6,563.53 in guardian ad litem fees, $4,460.37 for medical and dental expenses, and $15,000 in attorney's fees.The court directed Brian to pay $1,000 every month until the debt was cleared. An amended order in January 2019 retained this requirement and added conditions relating to employment updates, communication with Patricia and counselling for their child.Patricia continued seeking enforcement of the order, alleging that Brian had missed payments and failed to follow other directions. Both former spouses eventually became involved in bankruptcy proceedings.In October 2023, Brian asked the trial court to declare the contempt judgment satisfied. He argued that a $20,000 payment to Patricia's bankruptcy trustee in November 2022 had settled the debts covered by the $243,780 judgment. He also claimed to have paid $57,000 in monthly instalments.Patricia disputed his claim. She argued that some child support and children's expenses were exempt from the bankruptcy settlement and remained payable.Court finds father cannot count earlier payments twiceThe trial court accepted Brian's argument and ruled that he had cleared the contempt judgment. It counted his $57,000 in instalments and separately found that he owed just $450 in unpaid child support.Patricia challenged the decision, arguing that the court had incorrectly adjusted Brian's earlier payments against the remaining debt.The appeals court found that the $57,000 represented 57 monthly payments made between May 2018 and January 2023. However, the bankruptcy settlement took place on November 1, 2022. Therefore, $55,000 had been paid before the settlement and only $2,000 afterwards.The judges said the earlier $55,000 had already reduced Brian's debt before the bankruptcy arrangement. He could not use those payments again to clear amounts that remained outside the settlement.The court calculated that $1,006.32 of the earlier payments had gone towards the $4,460.37 in medical and dental expenses, leaving $3,354.05 unpaid.It also found that $3,384.20 had gone towards the original $15,000 attorney's fee award, leaving $11,615.80 outstanding.Together, the unpaid amounts came to $14,969.85. After deducting the $2,000 paid following the bankruptcy settlement, the court found that Brian still owed $12,969.85.$43,500 child support claim to be examined againThe appeals court also addressed a separate bankruptcy document submitted by Patricia. It showed that $43,500 of her claims relating to child support and children's expenses had been treated as exempt from the bankruptcy settlement.The lower court had refused to consider the document because the copy submitted during the hearing did not carry the bankruptcy judge's signature. The appeals court said Patricia should have been allowed to submit a signed copy.However, it clarified that the exemption did not establish that Brian automatically owed $43,500. It only protected Patricia's right to pursue the claim and retain any money recovered. The actual amount due still had to be determined.Patricia had also alleged that Brian misrepresented his financial position during the bankruptcy proceedings to secure the settlement. The appeals court did not decide this issue, saying allegations of fraud before a bankruptcy court had to be addressed by that court.The judges also rejected Patricia's request to seek an arrest or commitment order in the present proceedings over Brian's alleged failure to follow non-financial conditions of the contempt judgment. They noted that the children had become adults and some requirements could no longer be fulfilled. However, Patricia remained free to pursue other legal remedies.The appeals court reversed the finding that Brian had purged his contempt and directed the lower court to record the outstanding $12,969.85. It also asked the court to reconsider a commitment order, examine Patricia's request for attorney's fees and determine any additional child support or children's expenses due before March 19, 2019. The separate order requiring Brian to pay $450 in unpaid child support was upheld.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
