articles.title: Indian-origin Ohio mother sentenced to 90 days in jail three years after newborn daughter's body found in garbage truck. She says she did not know she was pregnant
articles.summary: An Ohio woman whose newborn daughter's body was found in a garbage truck more than three years ago has been sentenced to 90 days in jail and five years of
articles.body: An Ohio woman whose newborn daughter's body was found in a garbage truck more than three years ago has been sentenced to 90 days in jail and five years of probation. Anuradha Manukonda, 27, was sentenced on November 6 in Madison County Common Pleas Court after pleading guilty to gross abuse of a corpse, a fifth-degree felony, according to Local 12.The infant girl, later named “Madison Baby Doe” by the community, was discovered by garbage collection workers in the back of a truck in Plain City, Ohio, in June 2023.Manukonda's attorney told the court that she did not know she was pregnant and believed the baby was stillborn when she delivered her while visiting relatives in Plain City. According to the defence, she panicked following the delivery and placed the newborn in a garbage can.Garbage collectors who found the baby were traumatized; they quit their jobsProsecutors said the discovery had a profound impact on the two garbage collection workers who found the baby's body.“They quit their route. They quit that job. There was a group of Plain City residents who actually put together gift baskets for the two men ... because they were so traumatized and the residents felt so bad about what they went through,” one prosecutor said.The judge also addressed the impact of Manukonda's actions, saying: “The impact that you had on people went so far beyond what you could have been thinking at the time that you made those decisions.”Investigators faced difficulties determining how the infant died. An autopsy found extensive injuries, including fractures and lacerations, but the damage caused by the garbage truck's compactor and the delay in discovering the body made it impossible to establish the cause or time of death.Authorities said there was no evidence to establish that the baby's death was a homicide.Manukonda was identified as the child's biological mother through DNA evidence. Investigators collected samples from discarded items, including a beer bottle and a cotton swab, which helped link her to the baby.She was indicted in March 2025 and pleaded guilty in August 2026.Following the discovery, Plain City residents named the unidentified infant Madison Baby Doe and organized a funeral and burial for her.You use AI every day. articles.title: Karl Bushby spent 28 years making his way home; his final miles ended with an emotional reunion with the mother he hadn’t seen in a decade
articles.summary: After 28 years of walking across four continents, Karl Bushby reunites with his mother and family in an emotional homecoming in Hull, England, following his extraordinary journey from Chile.
articles.body: Angela Bushby had spent years thinking about what she would say when her son finally came through her gate. Ahead of his return, she told the BBC it would be a mock telling-off about the time. What she actually asked on November 2, 2026, was shorter. Karl Bushby, a 57-year-old former paratrooper, had just finished a 28-year journey from Punta Arenas, Chile, to the Hull house where he grew up. According to The Associated Press, Bushby covered about 31,000 miles across four continents and 30 countries, walking most of the route and swimming the major water crossings.Bushby left Punta Arenas in November 1998, hoping to finish in 12 yearsThe Goliath Expedition started on November 1, 1998. According to an Associated Press report published by ABC News, Bushby took a tent, a few hundred dollars and a cheap plastic camera. NPR indicated that he set two rules for himself: there would be no means of transport for advancing further and that he would not return to England until he got there on foot. According to the BBC, he estimated that his journey would last 12 years. The path included crossing the Darien Gap, the Bering Strait and the Caspian Sea.According to NPR, Bushby crossed the Darien Gap, the dense jungle that separates Panama and Colombia, between 2000 and 2001. NPR reported that in 2006, he crossed the frozen Bering Strait separating Alaska and Russia and indicated that it took him 14 days. He described it as the “crux of the entire journey.” Later in 2024, he swam across the Caspian Sea because other means of reaching Europe by land were closed. Al Jazeera further added that his journey also led him through Mongolia and China.Detentions, visa trouble and the 2008 financial crisis stretched 12 years into 28According to the AP, Bushby crossed the Bering Strait in 2006 together with fellow adventurer Dimitri Kieffer. After entering Russia illegally, the two were jailed and threatened with deportation. Earlier in 2001, in Panama, Bushby reportedly spent 18 days in prison because he had entered the restricted territory. In addition to this, money and paperwork issues led to a long delay. According to NPR, Bushby lost a sponsor due to the financial crisis of 2007 to 2008 and in 2012, he was not allowed to enter Russia with a visa. According to Explorerweb, the coronavirus pandemic added another delay: Bushby was stuck at the Iran border without a visa and had retreated to Mexico.Bushby crossed the English Channel in October 2026The final obstacle in the way of his journey was the English Channel. According to NPR, Bushby swam across it after he was refused permission to walk through the Channel Tunnel, which put him on British territory again after 28 years. According to the AP, his father, Keith, welcomed him on Dover Beach. Then Bushby continued his journey on foot towards the north of England.His mother embraced him outside her Hull home on November 2, 2026Hull City Council had asked the residents to join him in celebrating his return by meeting in Queen Victoria Square. According to AP News, he took his cart all the way to the City Hall, where many were there to greet him, before continuing with the last leg of the journey back to his mother’s home. There was a welcoming banner hanging right outside his mother’s house and according to AP, he embraced his crying mother amidst the cameras.BBC reported that his mother has seen him on only three occasions since 1998, the last about a decade ago. One such occasion was prior to the Bering crossing, where he had requested that they travel all the way to Alaska. AP reported that when Angela saw him, she asked, “Where have you been?” The line she had rehearsed for the BBC was “… and what time do you call this, Karl?” At the finish, Al Jazeera quoted Bushby crediting a team that he called “The biggest team. Earth.” The AP also reported that he reunited with his son, Adam, who is 36 and whom he had rarely seen. He also met his 12-year-old granddaughter for the first time. AFP reported that Werner Herzog is making a documentary about the trek and the six speaking engagements scheduled over the next two months.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 1968, a buried steamboat emerged from an Iowa mudfield, 30 feet down; its cargo of tools, clothes and food preserved a snapshot of life bound for Montana’s gold fields
articles.summary: In 1968, explorers uncovered the remains of the Bertrand, a steamboat that sank in 1865, revealing over 250,000 artifacts that illustrate life during the Montana gold rush.
articles.body: Treasure hunters who were searching the grounds of DeSoto National Wildlife Refuge in 1968 discovered evidence of a steamboat that had disappeared under the Missouri River more than 100 years ago. Nearly 30 feet below the surface, buried under layers of sand, silt, and dense blue clay, lay the Bertrand. The sternwheel steamer had sunk on April 1, 1865, while it was carrying commercial cargo from St. Louis to Montana. The commercial supplies on the ship included tools, clothing, food, household goods and equipment that were likely intended for growing gold-mining settlements around the region.Eventually, this discovery led to the recovery of more than 250,000 artifacts. Bertrand, unlike many other shipwrecks whose organic contents have deteriorated, preserved a notable range of everyday merchandise. The discovered supplies allowed the researchers to paint a better picture of how products were being transported towards the American West in 1865.A commercial shipment that was bound for Montana’s gold minesOn March 18, 1865, a newly loaded Bertrand departed the harbour of St. Louis under the command of Captain James Yore. The vessel was moving upriver towards Fort Benton in the Montana region, which was at the time considered an important trading point on the upper Missouri River. Despite the journey being a difficult one, steamboats provided a way of transporting huge quantities of provisions to frontier communities, military installations and mining camps. The shifting sandbars, changing channels and submerged obstacles made navigation along the Missouri particularly difficult.Alongside the common household supplies, mercury, known as quicksilver, was among the valuable materials aboard. It was considered valuable as it was used in gold extraction. The shipment reflected a demand for practical supplies in Montana’s growing mining settlements, where merchants relied heavily on river transport to bring goods from established trading centres farther east.About two weeks after leaving St. Louis, the steamer struck a submerged log, known as a snag, while it was travelling along the Missouri River north of Omaha. The impact damaged most of the vessel, and it sank near what is now the DeSoto National Wildlife Refuge. Archaeological accounts from the National Park Service note that the passengers and crew survived, but the boat and most of its remaining cargo were lost beneath the river. Initial operations reportedly recovered parts like its boilers and engine, while much of its merchandise remained underwater.How treasure hunters discovered the wreckAfter the sinking of Bertrand, the Missouri River did not remain in the same channel. Its shifting course and the sand movement alongside the silt slowly buried the wreck, and subsequent engineering work also altered the surrounding landscape. DeSoto National Wildlife Refuge was established in 1958, and in October 1960, the US Army Corps of Engineers completed the DeSoto Bend Cut-off Project. The wreck site lies within the refuge, close to the Iowa-Nebraska border.The search for Bertrand gained momentum in 1967, when Omaha-area treasure hunters Sam Corbino and Jesse Pursell obtained permission from the federal government to look for the vessel. They analysed historical documents and old river maps and used a fluxgate magnetometer to detect buried metal. In February 1968, test borings showed material from a large man-made object roughly 27 to 32 feet below the surface. Through the year, excavation crews removed the overlying earth, managed groundwater and slowly unearthed the hull.A preserved record of frontier commerceThe excavation revealed a shipment that went beyond just mining equipment. Researchers recovered barrels of flour and nuts, jars of honey, mustard, canned fruit, bottles of patent medicines, rolls of silk, shirts, coats and around thousands of shoes and boots. Furthermore, tools like axes, hammers, ploughs and mining implements were also found, as reported by Iowa PBS.The condition of the cargo was significant. Most of the material had been sealed inside the holds with tightly packed blue clay, thus restricting the movement of oxygen and slowing the deterioration of organic materials. Alongside the goods, labels and packaging also survived, thus allowing researchers to identify manufacturers, consignments and product types.Initially, the treasure hunters had hoped to find something valuable like gold and whiskey. However, the findings failed to match their expectations. No gold was found, and the whiskey did not prove to be the valuable cargo the searchers had anticipated. The greater discovery was the extensive collection of ordinary merchandise that had survived beneath the riverbed.Following the excavation, the artifacts underwent conservation, cataloguing and analysis before being prepared for storage and exhibition. Today, the DeSoto National Wildlife Refuge preserves a collection of more than 250,000 artifacts as noted by the US Fish and Wildlife Service. Selected objects can be seen in the refuge’s visitor centre.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A 197.80-carat sapphire once worn by Russia's last imperial family's dowager empress at a 1903 royal ball has sold for $4.9 million in Geneva, far above its presale estimate of up to $2 million
articles.summary: A 197.80-carat sapphire with a direct link to Russia’s imperial past has sold for $4.9 million at Sotheby’s in Geneva, far exceeding expectations.
articles.body: A 197.80-carat sapphire with a direct link to Russia’s imperial past has sold for $4.9 million at Sotheby’s in Geneva, far exceeding expectations. The stone, once part of the Russian Crown Jewels and worn by Dowager Empress Maria Feodorovna at the 1903 Winter Palace Ball, was offered as the centrepiece of a Cartier bracelet and had a presale estimate of up to 1.7 million Swiss francs, or roughly $2 million, as per Sotheby’s website.The sapphire, known as the Romanov Sapphire, carries a history that stretches back centuries. Its journey from the Russian imperial court to a modern auction room is a story of revolution, exile and reinvention, and its final sale price reflects the enduring appeal of objects with a royal past. Read more about it, as per the details on the auction house's website, here:A sapphire from the Romanov eraThe Romanov Sapphire is a 197.80-carat natural, unheated Ceylon sapphire, according to certificates from SSEF and Gübelin. Its unusual faceting style points to a Mughal-era origin, suggesting it may have entered the Russian Crown Jewels long before the Romanov dynasty reached its height.The exact date the sapphire entered the Russian Crown Jewels is not recorded. What is known is that it was part of a collection that included some of the most famous gemstones in history, many of which were acquired by Empresses Elizabeth and Catherine the Great in the 18th century.The stone was originally set in a diamond border by Fabergé and formed part of a pair of brooches or clasps, alongside a second sapphire weighing 249.25 metric carats. This pairing gave the sapphire a place in one of the most opulent royal collections ever assembled.Worn at the 1903 Winter Palace BallThe sapphire was worn by Dowager Empress Maria Feodorovna, born Princess Dagmar of Denmark, at the 1903 Winter Palace Ball in St Petersburg. She wore it on the front panel of her skirt, alongside its pair, in a costume that reflected the grandeur of the Tsarist court.The ball was a recreation of old Moscow, with the entire court dressed in 17th-century Moscovite style. The costumes were embedded with jewels sewn into the costumes themselves, a visual spectacle that captured the extravagance of the era.The image of the Dowager Empress in historicising Moscovite dress, adorned with large sapphires of old Mughal cutting style, became a lasting symbol of the Romanov court. It is this connection that gives the sapphire much of its historical weight today.From revolution to private handsAfter the Russian Revolution, the Soviet government inventoried the Russian Crown Jewels in a lavishly illustrated catalogue known as the Fersman catalogue. The collection was divided into three categories, with the most historically valuable pieces preserved and others sold abroad.The Romanov Sapphire fell into the third category, deemed to have little historical or artistic value beyond its intrinsic worth. It was sold off anonymously as part of the Soviet disposal of the Crown Jewels in the 1920s.In 1927, the sapphire was acquired by Ganna Walska, a socialite and self-proclaimed coloratura soprano known for her extravagant lifestyle and love of bold jewellery. She purchased it from Cartier, where it was set as the central pendant on a sautoir.Ganna Walska and the sapphire’s journeyGanna Walska was a larger-than-life figure who collected jewels with the same intensity she pursued marriages and artistic ambitions. She had the sapphire remounted in 1929 on another sautoir necklace, alongside a carved Mughal emerald weighing 256.60 carats.The necklace was altered many times over the years. By the time the sapphire appeared in Walska’s estate sale at Sotheby’s Parke Bernet in 1971, it was the centrepiece of a shorter necklace made of tumbled sapphire beads.The sapphire resurfaced again at Sotheby’s Geneva in 1992, this time set on an emerald and sapphire bead torsade necklace. Each iteration reflected the changing tastes of its owners and the evolving styles of the jewellery world.A modern Cartier braceletIn 2015, Cartier created the bracelet that now holds the Romanov Sapphire. The design echoes the Art Deco style that was in vogue when Cartier first mounted the sapphire for Walska in the 1920s.The bracelet features brilliant-cut diamonds and modified shield step-cut diamonds, with an interchangeable engraved rock crystal centre embellished with triangular diamonds. This design allows the sapphire to remain the focal point while adding a contemporary touch.The bracelet is signed Cartier and comes with case, pouches and documentation, including Cartier information bundles and copies of the original design. These details add to the piece’s provenance and appeal to collectors.Why the price exceeded expectationsThe sale price of $4.9 million was well above the presale estimate of 850,000 to 1.7 million Swiss francs. This suggests that buyers saw more in the sapphire than just its size and quality.The combination of imperial provenance, royal wear and a connection to one of the most dramatic periods in Russian history gave the stone a story that few modern gems can match. Collectors are often willing to pay a premium for objects with a documented past.The story behind the sapphire adds layers of narrative too, the gem itself, of course, but also part of the Russian Crown Jewels, worn by a dowager empress and then owned by a famous socialite.Marketplace NarrativesThe Romanov Sapphire’s strong result is indicative of a broader trend within the jewelry market.Buyers are increasingly drawn to items with a clear provenance, particularly those linked to royalty, famous collections or significant historical events.And the sale also shows that even stones once considered less historically significant can still command big prices if they have a good story behind them. The Romanov Sapphire was initially sold off anonymously by the Soviets, but its later journey gave it a new kind of value.The sapphire is much more than a piece of jewelry for the purchaser. It is a link to a vanished world, a tangible connection to the grandeur and tragedy of the Russian imperial court.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Did RFK Jr 'lie' to Congress about Samoa trip? Trump's health secretary faces probe over 'emboldening' anti-vaccine activists
articles.summary: Two Democratic senators are launching an investigation into whether US health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr “lied” to Congress about the reasons behind
articles.body: Two Democratic senators are launching an investigation into whether US health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr “lied” to Congress about the reasons behind his 2019 trip to Samoa, during his confirmation hearing.On Wednesday, Democratic Senator Ron Wyden of Oregon, who is set to take over as chair of a powerful Senate committee, wrote to Children’s Health Defense (CHD), a non-profit organisation known for its anti-vaccine activism that Kennedy chaired before joining the Trump administration. Wyden sought a wide range of documents related to Kennedy’s trip to Samoa, his 2024 presidential campaign, and his Senate confirmation process.“We are beginning an investigation into evidence that secretary of health and human services Robert F Kennedy Jr unlawfully lied to Congress on multiple occasions,” Wyden said in his letter, according to The Guardian.The letter was also signed by Angela Alsobrooks, a Democratic senator from Maryland.Kennedy was confirmed as health secretary in February 2025, joining President Donald Trump’s second administration. The health secretary, a nephew of former US President John F Kennedy, secured 52 votes in favour and 48 against. He has denied lying during his confirmation hearing.The controversyThe controversy centres on Kennedy’s 2019 visit to Samoa, which took place just months before a measles outbreak killed 83 people in the Pacific island nation, most of them children under the age of five. He travelled to Samoa in his capacity as chair and chief legal counsel of CHD. Critics, including Samoan officials, have alleged that his presence on the island “emboldened” anti-vaccine activists in the country, worsening a vaccination crisis.Kennedy has denied the allegations, including during two confirmation hearings in January 2025, maintaining that his visit had "nothing to do with vaccines."However, The Associated Press and The Guardian reported in August that Kennedy had sent a letter to Samoa’s prime minister on official CHD letterhead, in which he mentioned “vaccine” or “vaccination” eight times.“We are deeply concerned by the tactics Kennedy has used – both before and during his tenure as secretary – to stand in the way of children receiving life-saving vaccinations. In Samoa and in the United States, unvaccinated children have died tragic and preventable deaths during measles outbreaks.“We intend to hold secretary Kennedy accountable for the grave harm he has caused to vulnerable children. We also intend to hold him accountable for any false statements made to Congress, a crime that undermines the Senate’s ability to fulfil its constitutional duties,” senators Wyden and Alsobrook wrote in their letter to CHD.Like Kennedy, his department of health has also maintained that his 2019 visit to Samoa was "unrelated to vaccines."What nextDemocrats are set to regain control of Congress in January next year following their victory in the November 3 midterm elections. However, legal experts say the justice department under Trump is unlikely to prosecute Kennedy. They note that his statements could nevertheless provide grounds for congressional hearings, an impeachment inquiry or other efforts to challenge the Trump administration.Although prosecutions are rare, knowingly providing materially false testimony to Congress is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment.(With AP inputs)You use AI every day. articles.title: Two Iranian men convicted of spying for Tehran in UK
articles.summary: Two Iranian men have been convicted of spying on journalists in London, conducting surveillance for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The case highlights escalating threats from Tehran against those critical of the regime.
articles.body: Two Iranian men have been convicted of spying on journalists working for a Persian-language broadcaster in London after prosecutors established that they conducted surveillance on individuals critical of Tehran and gathered information that could assist Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).Mostafa Sepahvand, 41, and Farhad Javadi Manesh, 46, were found guilty at Woolwich Crown Court on Thursday following a six-week trial. A third defendant, Shapoor Qalehali Khani Noori, 57, was acquitted of all charges, according to AP.The prosecution said the two men carried out surveillance on journalists from Iran International, including Mojtaba Pourmohsen and Kambiz Hosseini, as well as Jonathan Turner, a founding member of UK Lawyers for Israel. The broadcaster is banned by the Iranian government.According to prosecutors, Sepahvand and Manesh visited locations associated with their targets, recorded photographs and videos, and used online platforms, including ChatGPT, to gather information about them.Frank Ferguson, chief prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service's special crime and counter-terrorism division, described the activity as a planned intelligence-gathering operation against people critical of the Iranian government.He said the defendants had been offered rewards for passing information to Iran, adding that Sepahvand was prepared to move beyond surveillance and carry out serious violence against those being monitored."Thankfully, the defendants were stopped before any attack could take place," Ferguson said.The convictions relate to conduct intended to assist the IRGC, which the UK proscribed in July under new legislation aimed at addressing threats from foreign states. Supporting or assisting the organisation can carry a prison sentence of up to 14 years.London's Metropolitan Police said the case was the fourth in recent years involving a direct threat to journalists associated with Iran International. The force said it was continuing efforts to protect those targeted.Vicki Evans, a deputy assistant commissioner at the Metropolitan Police, said hostile-state threats against the UK were increasing and that Iran was changing how it used intermediaries to carry out operations.She said authorities had encountered individuals travelling to Britain specifically to commit crimes before leaving, as well as British citizens and Iranian nationals with settled immigration status being used in such activities.The case comes amid wider counterterrorism investigations into suspected Iranian-linked operations in Britain. Police have examined possible connections between Iranian proxies and several incidents, including an arson attack earlier this year on four ambulances belonging to a Jewish community organisation in London.Iran has also been linked to an alleged plot targeting a US-operated military air base in England. The Iranian Embassy in the UK has rejected allegations that Tehran was involved in violent activities or incidents in the country.Sepahvand and Manesh are due to be sentenced at the Old Bailey, formally known as London's Central Criminal Court, on December 17.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Australian court awarded $1.346 million against the estate of a man convicted of abusing a foster child decades earlier; on November 11, the High Court set aside that outcome and ordered a new trial
articles.summary: Australia’s High Court has ordered a retrial in a damages case involving the estate of a man convicted of sexually abusing a former foster child decades
articles.body: Australia’s High Court has ordered a retrial in a damages case involving the estate of a man convicted of sexually abusing a former foster child decades earlier. The decision sets aside a previous award of $1.346 million and sends the matter back for a fresh hearing, leaving the claim unresolved for now, as per their website.The case, Estate of Croft v MTH, centres on a woman who was abused as a child while in foster care. She sought damages from the estate of the man convicted of the abuse, but the legal path to that outcome proved far more complicated than expected. Read more details about it, as per Australia’s High Court and Court Cart, here:How the case unfoldedThe woman, identified in court documents as MTH, represented herself during the original trial. She claimed that the man, whose estate she was suing, had sexually abused her while she was in foster care.The estate denied the allegations. The trial judge ultimately dismissed her claim, concluding that the evidence did not establish that the abuse had occurred.A key issue was how the court treated the man’s prior criminal convictions. The trial judge decided that the Evidence Act prevented those convictions from being used to prove the underlying abuse.The role of the convictionsThe man had been convicted of sexual offences against MTH. The question was whether those convictions could be used as evidence in a separate civil claim for damages.The trial judge took a narrow view, reasoning that the Evidence Act blocked the convictions from proving the acts themselves. This interpretation effectively removed a major piece of evidence from the case.The New South Wales Court of Appeal later reversed that decision. It held that the trial judge had made an error in how he applied the law, and it went on to decide the case as though a conviction certificate had been formally tendered.The appeal court’s approachThe Court of Appeal accepted that the abuse had occurred and reassessed the damages. This led to the award of $1.346 million against the estate.However, the High Court found that the appeal court had gone too far. It said the Court of Appeal effectively imposed an obligation on the trial judge to supply legal arguments for an unrepresented litigant, which was not required under the law.The High Court also objected to the fact that the appeal court decided the case based on evidence that had not been formally tendered during the original trial. This, it said, created a procedural problem that could not be ignored.What the High Court decidedThe High Court unanimously allowed the estate’s appeal in part. It agreed that the trial judge had misunderstood sections 91 and 92 of the Evidence Act, and that evidence of the convictions was in fact admissible to prove the acts to which they related.But the court stopped short of reinstating the damages award. Instead, it held that the Court of Appeal had erred in how it handled the case, particularly in relation to the unrepresented litigant and the use of untendered evidence.The result is that the claim is still open. The High Court has ordered a retrial, meaning the matter will be heard again from the beginning.Why this is important to unrepresented litigantsOne of the most important things about this case is that it involves pro se litigants.In the original proceedings MTH was self-represented, which placed her in a weak position to understand and apply the complicated legal rules.The High Court’s ruling clarifies that while courts must ensure a fair hearing, they are not required to act as legal advocates for parties who choose to represent themselves. This distinction is important, as it sets a boundary on how far judicial support can extend.The court at the same time accepted that the trial judge had bona fide erred in his construction of the Evidence Act. This means the retrial offers a chance for the case to be decided on a more accurate legal footing.What followsThe key issue in the retrial will be whether the abuse occurred and, if so, what damages should be paid.The convictions will now be considered admissible evidence, which could greatly bolster MTH’s case.The estate will have another chance to contest the claim and the High Court’s guidance will require the court to look closely at the evidence.The road ahead for MTH remains a difficult one. But the High Court’s ruling has given her case a second chance, and it has also clarified important legal principles that could affect similar cases in the future.You use AI every day. articles.summary: Barmer police probe patwari accused of raping an agriculture supervisor after posing as an RAS aspirant and threatening to leak videos; case filed Nov 7.
articles.body: Jaisalmer: Barmer police launched an investigation after a patwari allegedly raped an agriculture supervisor, a widow, after luring her with the promise of marriage by posing as an aspiring Rajasthan Administrative Service (RAS) candidate.In her complaint lodged at Women Police Station on Nov 7, the victim alleged that the accused, identified as Kesha Ram, took her from Barmer to Balotra and sexually assaulted her at a resort near Nakoda after mixing an intoxicating substance in her cold drink. He subsequently threatened to circulate her obscene videos and photographs on social media to blackmail her.Sarita Vishnoi, station house officer of Women Police Station, said a case had been registered against Ram based on the victim’s complaint. The police are completing the process of the victim’s medical examination and recording her statement. Police are also examining CCTV footage from the resort, digital conversations and call detail records, she said.The woman met the patwari during a crop-cutting survey. When she told him that she was a widow whose husband had died after their marriage in childhood, he allegedly offered to arrange her marriage with a young man preparing for the RAS exam.According to the complaint, on Oct 9, the patwari called her to Barmer, claiming that he would introduce her to an RAS aspirant. He later told her that the bus had broken down and that she would have to accompany him to Balotra. The two travelled in his car. He allegedly took her to a resort near Nakoda where he raped her.Fearing social stigma and humiliation, she did not initially disclose the incident to anyone. Both returned to Barmer the following day, Oct 10.The woman alleged that the patwari continued communicating with her over phone calls and chats by impersonating a person named Rahul, who was supposedly preparing for the RAS exam. articles.body: Ludhiana: A youth was found dead inside a room at a village crematorium near Jodhan, with a plastic bag allegedly stuffed in his mouth, leading police to arrest his friend on a murder charge.The deceased, Karanveer Singh alias Gopi of Mandi Latala village, had left home around 7pm on Nov 10 on his Activa scooter to buy household items but did not return.Police said his family searched for him at several places, including Dana Mandi Latala, before approaching his friend Gurkirat Singh alias Ravi to ask about his whereabouts. Gurkirat reportedly told them he did not know where Karanveer was and joined the family in the search.While heading towards Mandi Ahmedgarh, the family checked the village crematorium and found Karanveer lying face down inside an open room. When they turned him over, they allegedly found a white plastic bag stuffed in his mouth. A wooden stick was also lying nearby.The family rushed Karanveer to a doctor, who declared him dead.In his complaint, Karanveer’s father alleged that Gurkirat suspected his son of being in contact with his sister and that this had led to a dispute between the two. He alleged that Gurkirat, along with his associates, had beaten his son to death or got him killed.Police registered a murder case on the basis of the complaint and launched an investigation.Chappar police post in-charge ASI Jaspal Singh said Gurkirat was arrested from the village Wednesday evening. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday described bulldozers as a “brand” associated with Uttar Pradesh and suggested that CNH Industrial, a company setting up a tractor manufacturing plant in Gautam Buddh Nagar, should also consider manufacturing bulldozers in the state.The bulldozer has emerged as a potent political symbol of the Yogi Adityanath-led BJP government in Uttar Pradesh, representing its “tough-on-crime” and “anti-encroachment” image. It has also become a rallying point for supporters and a subject of opposition criticism over alleged selective demolitions.“You must have heard about Uttar Pradesh's bulldozer. I would like to tell CNH that since you are manufacturing tractors in Uttar Pradesh, you can also manufacture bulldozers here. There will automatically be demand for them in the country and abroad because it has already become a brand here,” PTI quoted the chief minister as saying.Yogi Adityanath was virtually addressing the ground-breaking ceremony of CNH Industrial's tractor manufacturing plant in Sector 8D of the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority area.Making a pitch for the state's improved law and order situation, he said Uttar Pradesh, which had faced questions over “neglect, backwardness and lawlessness” before 2017, when the BJP returned to power, had transformed from a “state of unrest” into one of celebration under the guidance of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.“Uttar Pradesh has moved from the rule of mafia to the rule of law,” he added.He attributed the improvement in law and order not only to police recruitment and modernisation but also to the BJP government's “zero-tolerance” policy towards crime and criminals.Yogi Adityanath noted that a strong law and order environment had helped the state emerge as a destination for ease of doing business, fearless business and investor confidence.He further stated that companies from India and abroad were now lining up to invest in the state, which had established a new identity as one of the country's major investment destinations.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Sonia has right to tell her story after years of BJP-RSS lies: Priyanka
articles.summary: Priyanka Gandhi says Sonia Gandhi has the right to tell her story in memoir amid BJP-RSS criticism; backs peaceful protests and questions ethanol blending.
articles.body: Kozhikode: AICC general secretary and Wayanad MP Priyanka Gandhi on Thursday said her mother Sonia Gandhi had every right to narrate her life story after years of what she described as lies and fabricated allegations spread by the BJP and RSS.“For the whole of my mother’s adult life in India, the BJP, the RSS have said whatever they wanted about her. They have told lies, they have fabricated stories, they have completely invented things, and she has been completely quiet. Now she is telling her story. She has a right to tell her story,” she said, responding to questions about the BJP’s reaction to Sonia’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, during her visit to Wayanad on Thursday.Priyanka said her mother had presented her perspective and explained what she wanted to convey through the book. “Anyway, I am very happy that they (her detractors) are reading her book,” Priyanka said after visiting the house of Padma Shri Cheruvayal Raman, who died recently, near Mananthavady.On the controversy over ethanol blending in petrol, Priyanka said people across the country were paying more and questioned the govt’s accountability on the issue.“The problem is that this govt thinks it is not accountable to the people for anything. When people, especially young people, ask questions, protest and demand answers, they try to silence them by beating them, putting them in jail and stopping protests. This is not a democracy. In a democracy, the govt is accountable for its every single action and that is what our Constitution says,” she said.Asked about the police action against S Valarmathi, secretary of the All Kerala Lower Primary School Teacher (LPST) Rankholders’ Association, and the dismantling of the protesters’ shed outside the Secretariat, Priyanka said people had the right to protest and should be allowed to exercise that constitutional right.“If there is violence, police should take action because they have to respect the rule of law. articles.title: Karnataka sets Rs 7.5 lakh crore investment target for 2027-30; Global Investors Meet from April 20
articles.summary: Karnataka targets Rs 7.5 lakh crore investment and 20 lakh jobs by 2030; Global Investors Meet 2027 in Bengaluru April 20-22, with new land bank, policies.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Karnataka has set an ambitious target of attracting investments worth Rs 7.5 lakh crore and generating 20 lakh jobs by 2030, with the next edition of the Global Investors Meet (GIM) scheduled to be held at Bengaluru’s Palace Grounds from April 20 to 22, 2027.Announcing the dates at the curtain-raiser event on Thursday, industries minister M B Patil said the govt was preparing to make the three-day event a truly global initiative, with a series of international outreach programmes to take Karnataka’s investment opportunities directly to investors in their respective countries and markets. As part of the preparations, govt unveiled the Aerospace and Defence Policy 2026-31 and launched the KIADB Digital Industrial Land Bank along with the third edition of VentuRISE.“Although the digital land bank and VentuRISE initiatives serve different purposes, they complement each other. One focuses on building the companies of tomorrow, while the other makes it easier to establish those businesses today. Together, these initiatives capture the central idea behind the Global Investors Meet 2027 — backing ambition with effective implementation,” Patil said.Highlighting the progress made since the previous GIM in 2025, he said Karnataka had received investment commitments worth approximately Rs 10.27 lakh crore, exceeding govt’s expectations. Around 65% of the manufacturing investments had already been converted into projects, with land allotments, approvals and construction progressing across the state. “The real measure of the success of an investors’ meet is not the day the MoUs are signed, but the day the factories begin operations,” he said.Investments by companies such as DN Solutions, Krones, Nidec and Foxconn had become operational in record time, while major projects by Lam Research, Applied Materials, MV, Wipro Electronic Materials, Jindal Aluminium and Mahindra Aerospace were progressing. The govt will also organise a dedicated investors’ conclave in North Karnataka to showcase opportunities in Kalyana Karnataka and Kittur Karnataka regions. “We want these regions to attract investments on a scale they have never witnessed before,” he said.Chief minister D K Shivakumar, inviting domestic and international investors to partner with Karnataka, said the state was positioning itself as a leading destination for semiconductors, aerospace, space technology, artificial intelligence, clean energy, life sciences and electric mobility. “This is not just an investment summit. It is an opportunity to shape Karnataka’s future. Bring your ideas. Bring your investments. We will build the future together,” he said.Highlighting the state’s economic performance, Shivakumar said Karnataka’s economy grew by 8% last year, outperforming the national growth rate. The state had the highest per capita income among India’s major states and the second-highest GST collections after Maharashtra. Karnataka attracted nearly USD 13 billion in foreign direct investment last year and is home to more than 1,100 global capability centres (GCCs), the highest in the country. It contributes over 40% of India’s software exports, while nearly two-thirds of the country’s aerospace exports originate from the state, he said.Under the Industrial Policy 2025-30, govt has set the target of attracting Rs 7.5 lakh crore in investments and creating 20 lakh jobs. The Aerospace and Defence Policy 2026-31 aims to attract Rs 60,000 crore and generate 60,000 jobs, while the Textile and Apparel Policy 2026-31 targets Rs 20,000 crore in investments and five lakh jobs.To encourage industries in backward regions, eligible units will receive additional incentives, including capital subsidies of up to 20% in the most backward and priority taluks. Shivakumar said the next phase of Karnataka’s economic growth would extend beyond Bengaluru to Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Belagavi, Tumakuru and Kalaburagi. Govt is promoting at least five industrial and innovation clusters outside Bengaluru, besides strengthening industrial parks, roads, logistics and regional connectivity.On infrastructure, he said the 2026-27 state budget had earmarked Rs 84,567 crore for capital expenditure, with investments planned in roads, railways, airports, industrial land, reliable power supply, Metro expansion and the Bengaluru Suburban Rail project. He also said nearly 70% of Karnataka’s installed power capacity came from renewable sources, adding that govt was expanding solar and wind generation and focusing on energy storage. “We want Karnataka to be not just an industrial hub, but a clean industrial hub,” he said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: Content distribution firm founder loses ₹34 lakh in APK fraud
articles.summary: Hyderabad founder loses ₹34.4 lakh as fraudsters use malicious APK to access phone and make 8 unauthorised credit card transactions; Cyberabad police register case.
articles.body: Hyderabad: The founder of a city-based content distribution company has lodged a complaint with Cyberabad police alleging that fraudsters accessed his phone through a malicious APK file and used his credit card details to siphon off ₹34.4 lakh.The complainant, a Kondapur resident, said he had been using an American Express credit card for several years, with his accountant regularly clearing the dues on the seventh of every month.“While reviewing the credit card statements I noticed unauthorised transactions totalling Rs 34.4 lakh. The amount had been debited from my credit card towards an e-commerce company without my knowledge or consent,” the complainant alleged.The complainant told police that eight fraudulent transactions occurred between April 29 and Nov 3, which he had never authorised. “I did not receive any OTPs or notifications regarding those transactions. When I examined my phone, an APK file was found, which the fraudsters apparently exploited to carry out the unauthorised transactions,” the complainant told police.The victim lodged a complaint on Nov 6. articles.title: Mischievous accounting, Karnataka manufactured 84% lie: MP Surya
articles.summary: BJP MP Tejasvi Surya disputes Karnataka Congress claim Centre funded only 16% of Bengaluru Metro, saying loans were miscounted; govt alleges speech cut at Pink Line event.
articles.body: Bengaluru: A day after the Congress govt claimed the Centre’s share in capital infusion for Bangalore Metro project plummeted to 16% over years, BJP Thursday argued the 84% figure was arrived at by wrongly counting BMRCL loans as the state’s contribution.Ahead of the inauguration of Namma Metro’s 7.5-km elevated Pink Line stretch between Kalena Agrahara and Suddaguntepalya by PM Modi on Friday, BJP claimed the financing pattern for Bangalore Metro is 54:46, contrary to Congress govt’s 84:16 calculation.Bangalore South MP Tejasvi Surya accused the Congress govt of indulging in ‘credit chori’ and alleged nearly Rs 29,000 crore in foreign loans provided to BMRCL by international financial institutions, backed by the Centre’s sovereign guarantee, had been included in the state’s contribution to project Karnataka govt’s share as substantially higher.“This money is routed to BMRCL, which is also responsible for repaying loans. Where is the state govt’s contribution to this? They are misleading the public through mischievous accounting,” Surya said.BJP’s response came after Greater Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda stated that of the total Namma Metro project cost of Rs 77,891 crore, the state govt had contributed Rs 65,291 crore, while the Centre’s contribution stood at Rs 12,600 crore.Surya argued BMRCL, a special purpose vehicle, was a separate entity and its borrowings should not be treated as direct state govt expenditure.Excluding loans from the state’s contribution, its share would fall to 46.6%, while the remaining 53.4% would include Centre-backed institutional financing and other funding, Surya claimed.On the state govt bearing expenses towards land acquisition, rehabilitation, grants-in-aid and other components, Surya said these were part of the agreed funding arrangements and were not exclusive to Karnataka.On the proposed Red line (Sarjapur-Hebbal), Surya rejected the state govt’s charge that the Centre had delayed approval for more than 22 months. He said the Centre had scrutinised the detailed project report and reduced the proposed cost from Rs 28,405 crore to Rs 25,999 crore, resulting in a saving of Rs 2,406 crore.On Orange line, Surya accused the state govt of delaying implementation by repeatedly changing the design.Surya said the elevated corridor of Pink line had received central approval in 2014, but the then Congress govt awarded the construction contract only in 2017.You stop my speech, but you can’t stop my work: KBGBengaluru: Greater Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda Thursday alleged he had been denied an opportunity to speak at the Pink line inauguration at the IIMB auditorium because he demanded justice for Karnataka.The minister was referring to a skewed Centre-state contribution to Namma Metro projects.On X, he said, “You may cut my speech, but you cannot stop me from working for Bengaluru’s development. We’ll continue our work with even greater commitment.”Byre Gowda said his speech, included in the draft programme, was excised late night.According to the final programme schedule, PM Narendra Modi, governor Sudha Yadav, chief minister DK Shivakumar and Bangalore South MP Tejasvi Surya will address the gathering.The PM is scheduled to travel by Metro from Suddaguntepalya to IIMB before inaugurating the 7.5-km elevated Pink line stretch and launching several other projects.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news.
